## Objective and scope

Publish the local release-readiness record, capability ledger update, reproduction runbook and maintenance decisions for the exact qualified revision.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Update capability status only from Q04/G5 evidence satisfying both the existing ledger and the stronger epic criteria. Document cohort/input operating range, uncertainty and remaining limitations.
2. Run required project/platform/consumer checks appropriate to changed code, including affected JVM/Scala.js tests and ownership validation; verify examples from a clean invocation.
3. Reconcile historical HalfFlow-CC G5/G6 and labeled-cohort P7 using explicit evidence crosswalks. Preserve historical receipts and do not automatically close broader or different architecture contracts.
4. Freeze supported API/policy/evidence versions and keep a reproducible control. Any postqualification numerical change reopens qualification; package publication is a separate authorized action.

## Planned areas

- docs/halfflow-capability-ledger.md
- docs/validation.md
- docs/benchmarks/real-world-registration.md
- reproduction documentation

## Blocking prerequisites

- G5 (`bd-01M4X4DXBQBXM8X5TYD157REDD`)
- U01 (`bd-01M4X4E04RDJ3NBEVA2ZNGSP6X`)
- U02 (`bd-01M4X4E0ADEA2KGZSVWDWZGG8C`)

## Evidence and safeguards

Use Mote claims/path reservations when implementation begins. Preserve unrelated dirty work and immutable historical studies. Reuse canonical providers and current owners. Keep labels/evaluation-only masks out of fitting, tuning on qualification data, and runtime stopping. Record exact source/provider/input/config identities, commands, numerical tolerances and all failures; run affected JVM/Scala.js and independent numerical checks. Current geometry/export thresholds cannot be relaxed to improve a pass rate. Completed research may be negative; milestone/epic acceptance remains a separate evidence-based decision.
